A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EDP-SAM/XMask research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original crowd segmentation and counting results, component ablations, efficiency measurements, and supplementary hyperparameter experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds segmentation comparison results for S4M and CrowdSAM in Table 1.

M1.justification: EDP-SAM, XMask, Gaussian smoothing, center sampling, and mask-constrained counting are retained. Equation (11) explicitly writes the center-feature distance already described in v1; it does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate crowd instance segmentation and counting on ShanghaiTech A, UCF-QNRF, and JHU++. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds S4M [61] and CrowdSAM [7], with NNEC marked for CrowdSAM, across the existing datasets and label percentages. Existing segmentation, counting, and ablation comparators are retained.

E3.justification: The 5%, 10%, and 40% labeled settings, metrics, preprocessing, training budgets, and existing evaluation controls remain unchanged. The added baselines use the existing comparison grid; the NNEC fairness clarification does not revise the previously reported FastSAM settings.

E4.justification: The component ablations, density-dependent efficiency analysis, hyperparameter studies, and EDP-SAM prompt/constraint comparisons are retained. Appendix analyses are unchanged, and Figure 6 merely highlights regions in existing examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. No statistical reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds nine scores each for S4M and CrowdSAM. For example, their ShanghaiTech A scores at 5% labels are 0.005 and 0.201, respectively. Existing Table 1 scores, counting results, ablation values, and supplementary findings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (11) expands the embedding term into an explicit L2 distance, consistent with v1's description and Appendix A.2 definition of center-feature distance. Removing the 'flat' subscript in Equation (10) and explaining the instance ID clarify notation; no substantive mathematical definition, assumption, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about mask supervision, segmentation efficiency, counting improvements, and state-of-the-art performance. The additional end-to-end training sentence repeats an existing claim.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 newly acknowledges possible evaluation circularity and argues that shared NNEC constraints and manually corrected annotations mitigate bias. Manual correction was already documented in v1; the new content is its interpretation as a fairness safeguard.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract. Appendix A's implementation, augmentation, optimization, training-budget, and threshold disclosures remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not verify the repository's contents.

R1.justification: The same 67 reference entries and research positioning are retained. Numerous entries receive publication and bibliographic metadata updates. S4M and CrowdSAM were already cited and discussed in v1; their new experimental participation is covered under E2.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose and notation clarifications, corrects typos and the author name Hongru Cheng to Hongru Chen, expands affiliations, adds acknowledgments, and updates bibliography metadata. The main narrative structure and appendix text remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains two rows and moves to page 13; Figure 8 moves to page 14. Figures 1–2 receive label edits, Figure 6 gains colored highlighting boxes, and table spacing changes. Appendix visual content is unchanged apart from headers.

improvement.justification: The additional S4M and CrowdSAM comparisons broaden empirical support, while the bias discussion, clearer energy notation, and code-access link improve transparency. These gains are limited: the new baselines receive little implementation detail, and the circularity discussion adds no independent validation. The core method, retained results, and appendix analyses remain unchanged.
